title: Quiesce protocol for partial-token handoff and client-timeout mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's streaming API must tolerate mid-generation client disconnects, transient network timeouts, and operator-driven cancellations without leaking GPU resources, leaving inconsistent cached prefixes, or losing durability for resumable generations. Existing heuristics (idle leases, TTL sweeps) reclaim resources but do not support negotiated handoff of partial token state to another client or allow short-lived resumability for structured outputs and tool-calls.

Objective:
Design and implement a 'quiesce' protocol that allows an active generation to enter a controlled partial-hand-off state when a client disconnects or signals a graceful stop, enabling: (1) short-window resumability (resume tokens with bounded TTL), (2) safe eviction and cleanup when resumptions do not occur, and (3) backpressure adjustments to avoid head-of-line blocking from stalled generations. The protocol should be compatible with structured-output and tool-calling flows (so that partial JSON / function-call states are checkpointed atomically).

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope: server-side runtime changes, API-level resume-token semantics, console metrics for partial generations, and integration tests + canary rollout.
- Non-goal: full multi-client collaborative editing of a single generation (out of scope). Long-term multi-client session work will be tracked separately.

Design summary:
1) Quiesce states: ACTIVE -> QUIESCED -> GC_PENDING -> GARBAGE_COLLECTED. QUIESCED holds a compact resume token (opaque id) + pointer to checkpointed KV cache slice and last structured-output checkpoint. TTL for resume tokens default=90s (configurable per-customer).
2) Checkpointing: At safe word boundaries (prefer token boundary or structured-object boundary), runtime snapshots: output prefix offset, minimal KV cache diff, tool-call invocation state (e.g., function name + partial args), and last emitted structured-output checksum. Snapshots are written to the metadata store (s3-backed index) and referenced by resume token. Snapshots size-limited and GC-able.
3) Backpressure integration: QUIESCED generations reduce priority in the batching scheduler and are marked as removable when scheduler needs capacity. ACTIVE generations keep affinity to current worker for low-latency continuation. QUIESCED items provide a quick-evict flag when memory pressure or low-latency SLOs for other customers require preemption.
4) API semantics: streaming client receives a final 'quiesce' event with resume_token and resume_ttl when the server transitions due to client disconnect or graceful stop. Resume endpoints accept token and optionally request strict sequence verification (for structured outputs).
5) Security/Isolation: resume tokens are opaque and short-lived. For private deployments, tokens can be customer-signed (HMAC) and validated by the private control plane.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server produces resume token on disconnect or explicit quiesce signal and stores snapshot within 2s of transition under nominal load.
- Resume within TTL returns consistent structured output up to last checkpointed boundary; tool-call continuations either resume or re-run deterministically as documented.
- Under load, QUIESCED generations can be reclaimed without affecting ACTIVE latency SLOs for other customers (verified by canary dashboard).
- Unit + integration tests cover checkpointing fidelity for streaming structured outputs and function-call boundaries.

Rollout plan:
- Feature branch + integration tests -> runtime PR -> internal canary on dedicated capacity -> staged rollout to 5% hosted customers with opt-in flag -> monitor metrics: resume_success_rate, quiesce_snapshot_latency, memory_reclaims_by_quiesce.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Quiesce+Protocol+Design
- Perf dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/streaming/partial-gen-sweeps
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7890
acceptance_criteria: 1) Resume tokens are emitted and stored reliably on disconnect/quiesce. 2) Resume attempts within TTL restore generation state matching the last checkpointed structured output. 3) QUIESCED generations are deprioritized by the scheduler and are evictable under memory/backpressure pressure. 4) No GPU memory leaks after GC_PENDING -> GARBAGE_COLLECTED cycle in extended soak tests.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial design proposal posted to Confluence. Emphasized atomic checkpoints for structured outputs to avoid partial JSON corruption on resume.
2026-03-04 - Design review (PM/Eng): Agreed on 90s default TTL but added config knob per-customer and per-model. PM (R. Kim) requested metrics for customer-visible resume failures.

2026-03-05 - Eng note (Liam O'Connor): Prototyped checkpoint write path using existing metadata-store APIs. Snapshot write adds ~1.1MB/sec overhead per concurrent quiesce under synthetic load. Need to compress diffs.
2026-03-07 - Security (M. Lopez): Reviewed token format. Proposed HMAC-signed tokens for Private deployments. No PII in checkpoints — confirmed.

2026-03-09 - Review feedback (Runtime team): Scheduler integration requires a new 'evictable' flag; split implementation into checkpointing + scheduler changes to reduce risk. Created follow-ups ENG-216010 (scheduler evictable flag).

2026-03-11 - QA (S. Wu): Integration tests added for function-call resume semantics. Found edge case: partial function args with streaming tool outputs may require re-execution of side-effectful tool calls. Decided to mark certain tool calls as non-resumable and emit explicit 'non-resumable' flag in resume metadata.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Opened PR #7890. Requesting review from infra and runtime performance owners. Added canary dashboard panel and smoke test script.
2026-03-12 - PM (R. Kim): Approved canary rollout schedule pending a green run on dedicated canary cluster and satisfactory memory-reclaim metrics.
